chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Salim (Abu al-Fadl), from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a female slave who has a husband. He said: 'It is not permissible for anyone to have sexual relations with her until her free husband divorces her.'

Therefore, this report is understood to mean that if the buyer acknowledges the husband and is satisfied with his marriage contract, because if the matter is as we stated, she is not permissible for him until he divorces her, nor is she permissible for anyone else either, unless he sells her in another sale. And that which indicates this is what we have previously mentioned from Bukayr ibn Ayn and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya.

key_terms.يَمَسَّهَا: to have sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man buying a married female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Tamlik al-Zawj* (acquiring the husband's right) in the context of purchasing a married female slave, establishing that the new owner is barred from intimacy until the free husband divorces her. The text notes that this ruling assumes the buyer acknowledges the existing marriage; if immediate access is desired, the alternative is to resell her to another party, a principle supported by earlier reports from Bukayr ibn A'yun and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya.
